cases.description: Blank lines between the heading and the text are not part of $body.
A line of only spaces or only a tab is a blank line (CommonMark 0.31.2, 2.1), so such lines before the text are removed as leading blank lines.
Spaces and tabs at the end of the last line, and the blank lines after it, are not part of $body, whether the body ends at a heading or at the end of the file.
$body is raw Markdown, so several blank lines between two paragraphs stay as they are.
Only the trailing whitespace of the whole $body is removed, so the two spaces of a hard line break and a tab at the end of an inner line stay.

cases.description: Only leading blank lines are removed, not the indentation of the first line, so an indented code block at the start of $body stays one (CommonMark 0.31.2, 4.4).
ATX headings need no blank lines around them and interrupt a paragraph (CommonMark 0.31.2, 4.2), so text on the line after a heading is its $body and ends at the next heading line.
A section's $body ends at its first child heading, and text after the child's heading belongs to the child until the next heading.
$body is raw Markdown, not an AST, so inline markup, a link, a task list and a table stay in their source form.
